methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Ark Electronics operates in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector at an undisclosed stage. The comparable universe consists of one public peer (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private companies, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. This fragmented landscape reflects the nascent and heterogeneous nature of frontier robotics ventures.

Standard peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. The Robotics & Manufacturing sector contains ten same-sector peers overall, but filtering for stage-specific, adjacent-stage, or valuation-tier-aligned comparables yielded fewer than three datapoints in any narrow category. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given the wide dispersion in business models, maturity, and capital requirements across robotics subsegments. Consequently, triangulation via conventional multiples-based methods cannot be reliably executed with the available dataset.

Without sufficient narrow peer cohorts or disclosed financial metrics for the target, a defensible quantitative valuation range cannot be supported by this analysis. Key uncertainties include the target's funding stage, revenue (if any), and burn profile—all of which would typically anchor stage-appropriate valuation methods. Further data collection on stage classification and a larger private peer dataset with disclosed terms would be necessary to enable triangulated analysis.
